Japan is one of the most creative countries in the world, and in this video, we explore three unbelievable things that make Japan truly unique. The first thing you’ll see is Japan’s famous artistic packaging. snippet.title: The haunting history of the Paris Catacombs - Stephanie H. Smith
snippet.description:
Take a tour of the vast, underground network of the Paris Catacombs, and find out how this 18th century cemetery came to be.

--

For centuries, Parisians had buried their dead in the Cemetery of the Innocents. By the 18th century, the grounds had become overcrowded — spewing foul odors across the city. Residents worried that it posed a public health threat, and petitioned the government for a solution. But where could they move millions of remains? Stephanie H. Smith explores the vast, underground network of the Catacombs.

An evil stepmother demands a maiden’s lungs and liver; a girl is ripped from a wolf’s stomach; and sisters mutilate their feet to squeeze into a gold slipper. During the early 1800s, brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm gathered these unflinchingly gory details from stories circulating around what’s now Germany. Claudia Schwabe explores how these now-infamous tales evolved as they spread worldwide.

snippet.title: Iran in the 1970s vs Now #comparison #history
snippet.description:
This archival footage shows Iran during the 1970s, prior to the events of the 1979 Islamic Revolution.
At the time, the country was undergoing rapid modernization under Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. Universities expanded, industrial development increased, and urban centers such as Tehran reflected significant economic and cultural transformation.

Women participated in higher education, professional careers, and public life, while secular legal reforms shaped governance and social institutions. Western cultural, architectural, and technological influences were visible in major cities, alongside traditional Iranian society.

The 1979 Revolution marked a major political and social turning point, leading to the establishment of the Islamic Republic and a restructuring of laws, institutions, and public life.

This video presents historical footage to document that earlier period through visual record.

snippet.title: The African Rulers Who Built the Slave Trade | History's Uncomfortable Truth
snippet.description:
Explore the untold story of the African Kingdoms that built the Slave Trade. For centuries, the narrative has been incomplete. In this documentary, we examine the complex history of West African empires like Dahomey, the Oyo Empire, and the Aro Confederacy, who became powerful economic and political forces through participation in the transatlantic slave trade.

Why did African rulers choose to participate? How did the trade of guns for people create a cycle of violence that reshaped the continent? We analyze the brutal calculations of power, survival, and empire-building that defined this era.

This video seeks to present the full, uncomfortable truth—not to assign blame, but to understand the mechanisms of history. By examining primary sources, including the desperate letters of Kongo King Afonso I, we restore agency to a history often oversimplified.

snippet.title: The incredible engineering of Venice - Stephanie H. Smith
snippet.description:
Explore the history of Venice to find out how the infamous floating city was built and how the republic became a hub for trade.

--

To escape Germanic invaders, people fled into the Venetian Lagoon in the 6th century. The settlers set out to tame the mudflats and built a foundation in the marshy maze to support heavier, longer-lasting structures. Little did they know, this system of wood, water, and mud would still be supporting an infamous floating city 1,500 years later. Stephanie H. Smith explores the history of Venice.
